newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Metals- Singapore copper, zinc stocks to rise.
newsitem.headline: Asia Metals- Singapore copper, zinc stocks to rise.

text.p: Copper and zinc stocks at the London Metal Exchange (LME) warehouse in Singapore are likely to climb further, putting pressure on already soft premiums here, Far Ease base metal dealers said on Friday.

Copper stocks at the LME's Singapore warehouse reached 39,275 tonnes on Thursday, up sharply from the 14,050 tonnes reported at the start of May. Zinc stocks rose to 36,750 tonnes compared with 12,700 tonnes in early May.
"I heard there might in excess of another 10,000 tonnes of copper going into the warehouse here," a senior dealer for a metal trading company told Reuters.

"I think there's more copper to be brought here. A lot of it is coming from China although it is not being shipped directly here. They're trying to take advantage of the high cash prices and the good backwardation since demand in China at this time is particularly low," said the general manager of a metal firm.
Traders said it makes sense to transfer the copper to Singapore rather than hold on to the metal during the slow summer holiday season in the United States and Europe.
Aside from China, copper was also coming into the LME's warehouse in Singapore from Long Beach, California.
Traders said the volume of copper still off-warrant in Singapore warehouses could range between 5,000-10,000 tonnes.
Zinc stocks are also tipped to rise with some dealers estimating that about 7,000-15,000 tonnes remain off-warrant in warehouses in Singapore.
With three-month zinc quoted near 6-3/4 year highs of about US$1,520 a tonne, Chinese merchants have moved thousands of tonnes here to take advantage of the strong prices and firm demand.
"The zinc stocks are still going up," a dealer said.
"There are continuing dribs and drabs of zinc coming here from China. We might see more zinc coming onto (LME) warrant," another trader said.
Abundant zinc and copper stocks piled on more pressure on already weak premiums for both metals, Far East dealers said.
"The premiums have dropped in line with the rise in stocks," one dealer said.
Premiums for Grade A copper cathodes slumped to $3-$10 a tonne against $25-$35 in mid-March. Premiums for 25-kg zinc ingots ranged from zero to $5.
"You can get as much material as you want for $1-$2," said Vinod Kumar of metal company Donald Mcarthy.
"Most people are delivering zinc at flat premiums," another trader said.
The only base metal providing joy is aluminium, where premiums eased slightly but remain strong on good regional demand.
"The demand is still there, but not as aggressively as two weeks ago," an aluminium dealer said.
Premiums in Singapore for western 20-25 kg ingots eased slightly to $80-$90 a tonne from last week's $80-$100, but tight supplies kept them at a high level.
Aluminium stocks reached 6,375 tonnes on Thursday from 15,825 tonnes at the end of April.
"The premiums have eased off a bit, but they are still strong premiums because they are reflecting the shortage of the material," a dealer said.
Premiums in Taiwan were seen at $90-$95 a tonne CIF Kaoshiung and Keelung, $90-$95 a tonne CIF Jakarta in Indonesia, and $95-$100 a tonne CIF Pusan in South Korea, dealers said.
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
